text:
maria_sales: Hey team — Poncho Health kickoff. They're doing a 2-week Private POC in their AWS account. Main asks: can we support BYO forward proxy (their corporate outbound proxy), do we provide static egress IPs for allowlisting, and what's our recommended connectivity: PrivateLink endpoint vs VPC Peering via TGW? Also they need a short firewall rules snippet for their security team. 

alex_se: Quick context: POC will run Redwood Private (control plane SaaS, compute in their VPC). They want model serving inside their VPC but egress must go via their existing proxy. No internet egress from subnets allowed except to their proxy.

sanjay_network: We support both patterns. Tradeoffs: PrivateLink keeps control-plane connectivity minimal (API/control via endpoint), VPC Peering/TGW gives lower cross-AZ latency and simpler routing for autoscaling. If they insist on traffic through corporate proxy, that works but we need a stable egress IP or an outbound proxy chain so their firewall can allowlist.

julia_infra: For static egress we can either: 1) use customer NAT gateway (preferred) so egress IPs are fully customer-controlled, or 2) provide redwood-managed egress IPs in the dedicated case (there's a small monthly charge + NAT gateway on our side). If they want to avoid inbound peering, PrivateLink for control plane + endpoints for model traffic is safest for restrictiveness.

maria_sales: @poncho_netops can you confirm if your proxy supports SNI passthrough for TLS CONNECT? If not we need to route by IP or do TLS termination which they typically won't allow.

poncho_netops: Our proxy allows TLS CONNECT + SNI, we can do allowlists by SNI+IP. We will need 3-4 IPs to add to the firewall; auditors want a small CIDR if possible. Also, SOC2 team asked for KMS integration and detailed access logs.

alex_se: Noted. For the firewall snippet, here's a minimal example you can drop into your change request: 

```
# Allow outbound to Redwood control plane (control plane endpoint FQNs provided during onboarding)
Allow TCP 443 to *.redwood-control.example.com (resolve to listed IPs)
# Allow outbound to model-serving egress (if using redwood-managed egress IPs)
Allow TCP 443 to 203.0.113.45
Allow TCP 443 to 203.0.113.46
# If customer NAT gateway is used, allow to your NAT IPs instead
```

sanjay_network: Important: if they're using SNI-based allowlist, we must ensure we don't multiplex multiple tenants over the same IP/CN in the POC. For Private deployments we can reserve per-customer egress IPs for POC windows.

kari_ae: Pricing note for the finance team: BYO-proxy + customer NAT = no extra redwood egress charge, standard Private plan applies. If customer asks for reserved redwood-managed egress IPs or a managed SNI proxy we add a small monthly fee plus per-GB transfer. I'll pull exact numbers and loop back.

julia_infra: Action items: (1) @poncho_netops share proxy FQDN and NAT IPs + preferred CIDR (2) @sanjay_network to confirm whether we can carve two reserved IPs for the 2-week POC (3) @kari_ae to send a short price delta for managed egress vs BYO-nat. We can target POC network runbook by EOD tomorrow.

poncho_netops: Sending proxy FQDN and egress NAT IPs now in a separate message. Also attaching brief excerpt from their security questionnaire: "Require IP allowlist, TLS 1.2+, KMS-backed key for model audit logs".

maria_sales: Thanks everyone — I'll consolidate and send the POC runbook to Poncho and schedule a network sync tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
